nodes.title: Kalman filtering with a packed state
widgets_values:
cv2.KalmanFilter is stateful - predict() and correct() mutate the object - so it cannot be a generated wrapper and it cannot hand a live handle across a graph edge either. 'CV Kalman Filter Step' packs the whole filter state (posterior vector + error covariance) into ONE NPARRAY: chain one node per frame, state output -> next frame's state input, and leave the first frame's state unconnected to initialise from the first measurement.

WHAT IS TRACKED: a red bicycle crossing pedestrian_area.mp4 left to right at a nearly constant ~16 px/frame. The measurement is a chained 'CV Track Window' (meanShift on a hue x saturation back-projection) seeded once on video frame 21 - so it follows ONE physical object instead of re-deciding every frame the way an argmax detector would.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR: from row 5 the bike passes behind pedestrians, the mean density under the window falls from ~23 to ~20, below the 22.2 threshold, and 'found' goes false. Track Window then ECHOES its input window - the red dot FREEZES at (509, 221) and is 56 px behind by the last row. The switch inside 'CV Hue Track Step' feeds the filter an EMPTY array on those frames, so it predicts only and the yellow dot coasts along the estimated velocity of ~16 px/frame, staying within ~10 px of the bike - 3 to 6 times closer than the stalled tracker. That is why 'measurement' is an optional SOCKET rather than an 'enabled' boolean widget.

The three markers are drawn LARGEST FIRST so none hides another, and it is the RADIUS that identifies them - r10 = raw measurement, r7 = filtered, r4 = prediction. Colour (vermillion / blue / yellow) only repeats what the size already says, so the picture still reads for a colour-blind viewer and in greyscale. Where they coincide you see one bullseye; where they separate, the story.

While the track IS locked the filter also beats the raw detector (0.3-5 px vs 3-5 px): the r7 marker sits closer to the bike than the r10 one.

Try: raise process_noise to follow abrupt manoeuvres, or measurement_noise to smooth harder and lag more. Switch the model to 'constant acceleration' for curved motion. The 'velocity' output draws with 'CV Draw Rays'.
